root_cause.text: The flow dissector (`__skb_flow_dissect`) attempts to parse PPPoE Protocol Field Compression (PFC) frames, which shifts the subsequent network header by one byte and triggers unaligned memory access exceptions on architectures that do not support unaligned access.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "having a compressed (1-byte) protocol field means the subsequent PPP payload is shifted by one byte, causing 4-byte misalignment for the network header and an unaligned access exception on some architectures." This is resolved in the patch by removing the code block in `__skb_flow_dissect` that handles compressed protocol fields (`ppp_proto & 0x0100`) and shifts `nhoff` by `PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1`.

intent_record.what: Removed the conditional block that handled PPP Protocol Field Compression (PFC) by shifting the protocol value and adjusting the offset, simplifying the code to always increment the offset by PPPOE_SES_HLEN.
intent_record.how: Prevents the flow dissector from processing compressed 1-byte PPP protocols, ensuring PFC frames fail the subsequent validity check and are rejected with FLOW_DISSECT_RET_OUT_BAD.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerable PPPoE Protocol Field Compression (PFC) parsing logic. Specifically, in lines 1234-1240, it checks if the protocol field is compressed (`if (ppp_proto & 0x0100)`) and, if so, decrements the offset shift by 1 byte (`nhoff += PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1;`). This shifts the subsequent network header offset by an odd number of bytes (7 bytes), leading to unaligned memory access on architectures that do not support it.

Specifically, the code block starting at line 1236 checks if the protocol field is compressed (ppp_proto & 0x0100) and, if so, shifts the network header offset (nhoff) by PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1 instead of PPPOE_SES_HLEN.
